title: Why Employers Can't Tame Health Costs
gist: RAND and USC researchers argue that price transparency hasn't let most employers control health costs: self-insured plans depend on third-party administrators whose fees (e.g., 'shared savings fees') misalign incentives, and insurer consolidation leaves few alternatives, so disclosure rules—including new 2026 PBM rules—need enforcement and competition fixes.

insights.claim: For a decade the federal response to rising employer health costs has been price transparency, but interviews with employers, consultants, administrators and experts indicate few employers beyond the very largest can turn price information into negotiating leverage.

insights.so_what: Transparency-based policy has not bent the cost curve; large employers retain an advantage over smaller ones.
